newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek strikes disrupt sea and air transport.
newsitem.headline: Greek strikes disrupt sea and air transport.

text.p: Greek seamen defied a court ruling declaring their walkout illegal on Friday and civil aviation staff joined in strikes that have disrupted Greece's air and sea transport.
Ships remained idle in ports for a fifth day while flights were cancelled or delayed at Greek airports, officials said.

The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) said they would pursue their strike, which is due to end on Tuesday and affects all ships with Greek crews, despite a Piraeus court order to return to work or face fines and detainement.

Shipowners had asked the court to declare the strike illegal, but federation spokesman George Maroulakis said: "The court ruling will not affect our movement. It will strengthen the seamen's reaction against the government and the conflict between the two will become sharper."
Striking seamen, who want better pensions, benefits and measures against unemployment, gathered at ports to stop any ships from docking or sailing but there were no clashes, the coast guard said.
Civil aviation staff also went on strike, disrupting flights at airports around the country, to protest against wage and bonus cuts.
Air traffic controllers held a four-hour work stoppage and plan to repeat it on Sunday between 1200 and 1600 GMT. Airport electrical engineers are due to begin a three-day strike on Saturday.
